<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

`/inference/v1/generate` with `output_mode: "derender"` now reports `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` in batch and stream mode, summed over the choices, as `/v1/chat/completions` does. Fixes #65360.

**Stacked on #64041.** The first commit (b5701018c5) is #64041 cherry-picked onto main; review only the commits after it (170677d681, 658be9d6a6). This PR reuses the reasoning-token count #64041 adds to `OnlineDerenderer._parse_and_assemble`, so it can't land first. I'll rebase once #64041 merges.

## Claims

- With `--reasoning-parser`, batch and stream generate derender usage include `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`. Before this change it was `null` on both paths.
- The count matches `/v1/chat/completions`, including with `include_reasoning: false` and summed across choices when `n > 1`. Stream with `n > 1` works here, unlike chat derender in #64041, because generate keeps a live parser per choice.
- Without a reasoning parser (or with only a tool parser), `completion_tokens_details` stays `null`, as on chat.
- `tokens` and `text` output modes are unchanged.

## Validation

**New end-to-end test (1x L4):** `test_derender_mode_usage_reports_reasoning_tokens` in `test_serving_tokens.py`. It starts a real server with Qwen3-0.6B and `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v3`, reusing the server fixture of the existing reasoning tests. It compares generate derender usage with `/v1/chat/completions` for batch with `include_reasoning: true` and for stream with `include_reasoning: false`. Both use `n=2` with seeded sampling (greedy rejects `n > 1`).

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py -k test_derender_mode_usage_reports_reasoning_tokens
```

Before (b5701018c5, #64041 only, with the new test file):

```text
E       AssertionError: assert None == {'reasoning_tokens': 62}
E       KeyError: 'completion_tokens_details'
2 failed, 26 deselected in 49.40s
```

After (this branch):

```text
2 passed, 26 deselected in 49.40s
```

Usage from the issue's repro request on the same server, run twice per mode; chat and generate matched on every run:

```text
batch,  include_reasoning=true:  chat and generate {'prompt_tokens': 16, 'completion_tokens': 64, 'completion_tokens_details': {'reasoning_tokens': 62}}
stream, include_reasoning=false: chat and generate {'prompt_tokens': 16, 'completion_tokens': 64, 'completion_tokens_details': {'reasoning_tokens': 62}}
```

**CPU unit tests (macOS):** both affected unit-test files pass.

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py \
       tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py
```

```text
183 passed, 1 xfailed in 213.75s
```

`pre-commit run` passes on the changed files. These tests run in CI in the `entrypoints-integration-api-server` step (`pytest entrypoints/scale_out`).

## Details

**Root cause:** `ServingTokens` built `UsageInfo` from token counts only, in `_build_response_fields` (batch) and in the final stream usage chunk. #63103 left `reasoning_tokens` out of scope.

**What changed:**
- **Batch:** `OnlineDerenderer.derender_text_choices` now also returns `completion_tokens_details`. It sums the per-choice count from `_parse_and_assemble` (#64041). It is `None` unless `--reasoning-parser` is set.
- **Stream:** `serve_tokens_stream_generator` keeps each choice's output token IDs. At the end, `OnlineDerenderer.stream_completion_tokens_details` counts them with that choice's `ChatStreamProcessor` parser. Coupled chat does the same.

**Limitation:** per-chunk `continuous_usage_stats` usage still has no details. Coupled chat recounts every token on every chunk to fill them; I left that out to keep this small. It's noted in the docs.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR references #65360 or touches generate usage. #64041 covers `/v1/chat/completions/derender` only and lists generate as out of scope. #64935 covers `/v1/chat/completions/batch` only.

nodes.body: Thank you @hickeyma , I will wait for #64041 before apply the changes. Should i handle ```continuous_usage_stats``` in another pr after both merged ?

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks @ldkhang1201 for picking this up. The fix looks right and covers what #65360 asked for. This has to wait for #64041 to land and then get a rebase. 

A few small suggestions:
- token_in_token_out/serving.py:756 keeps the output tokens even when there's no reasoning parser. Coupled chat only keeps them when the count gets reported, so the same guard would work here.
- The CompletionTokenUsageInfo block is repeated at online_derenderer.py:385 and :446 and could be a small helper.
- The e2e test never closes </think> within 32 tokens and the CPU helper hardcodes _include_reasoning_tokens_details = False. A stub parser unit test would be cheap and would cover both the closed block and the summing in the stream path.

Leaving continuous_usage_stats for a follow-up is fine.

@@ -116,7 +116,7 @@ The server keeps no state between calls. Everything the next call needs is in `s
 - **Echo `stream_state` back.** Leave it out (or send `null`) on the first call, then send the `stream_state` from each response with the next request, unchanged. State that doesn't add up (e.g. `output_chunk_lens` that don't sum to the number of output tokens) is rejected with a `400`.
 - **One choice per chunk.** `/inference/v1/generate` sends one choice per SSE event and each derender call accepts at most one. More than one is rejected with a `400`.
 - **`n > 1` is N streams.** Generate interleaves chunks for different choices and tags each with its `index`. Keep one `stream_state` per index and send each chunk with the state for its index. Each index gets its own `role` delta on its first chunk.
-- **Send every chunk through, including the last ones.** The finish reason usually arrives with the final tokens. A chunk with a `finish_reason` and no tokens is accepted too and flushes any buffered tool call arguments. With `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`, generate ends with a usage only chunk (`choices: []`). Send it through derender like any other chunk to get the usage chunk for the response. `usage.prompt_tokens` is the request's `prompt_tokens` if set, otherwise the generate chunk's.
+- **Send every chunk through, including the last ones.** The finish reason usually arrives with the final tokens. A chunk with a `finish_reason` and no tokens is accepted too and flushes any buffered tool call arguments. With `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`, generate ends with a usage only chunk (`choices: []`). Send it through derender like any other chunk to get the usage chunk for the response. `usage.prompt_tokens` is the request's `prompt_tokens` if set, otherwise the generate chunk's. `usage.prompt_tokens_details` is the generate chunk's. `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` is counted by the reasoning parser over the tokens in `stream_state` when one is configured, as on `/v1/chat/completions`. With `n > 1` it stays `null`: the usage chunk arrives with one index's `stream_state`, so the count can't cover every choice the way `completion_tokens` does.
 - **Send the same context on every call.** `chat_request` and `prompt_token_ids` aren't kept between calls, so they go with every chunk including the usage chunk. Both are required when a tool or reasoning parser is configured. `prompt_token_ids` is the `token_ids` of the `GenerateRequest` returned by `/render`.
 - **Send `prompt_token_ids` on the first chunk, even without a parser.** It seeds detokenization so the first token's leading space matches the coupled endpoint (see [Request format](#request-format)). Later chunks already carry that context in `stream_state`.
 - **Don't forward `[DONE]`.** It marks the end of the generate stream and isn't a chunk.

@@ -93,6 +93,7 @@ print(response["choices"][0]["token_ids"])
 - `parse_context` is ignored at other levels, so a rendered request can go to a prefill leg unchanged.
 - `logprobs` follow coupled chat. `top_logprobs` is cut to `sampling_params.logprobs`, `logprob_token_ids` is honored. When a parser hides the reasoning with `include_reasoning: false`, `logprobs`, `token_ids` and `sampling_mask` are dropped so they don't expose it.
 - `finish_reason` follows coupled chat too. It's `tool_calls` when the message has tool calls except with a named `tool_choice` or a `length` cut.
+- With a reasoning parser, `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` is the reasoning parser's count summed over the choices, as on coupled chat, also with `include_reasoning: false`. In a stream it's on the final usage chunk, not on per-chunk `continuous_usage_stats` usage.
 - With `stream: true`, each choice carries a chat `delta` (`role`, `content`, `reasoning`, `tool_calls`) instead of `text`, and `finish_reason` follows coupled chat. `role` is set on the first chunk of each choice, `n > 1` is supported, and `null` fields are left out of `delta`. A chunk is sent whenever the engine output carries a parsed delta, visible token IDs, logprobs or a `finish_reason`. Parsing runs on the API server event loop, so `--api-server-count` scales it.
 - Cohere grounding citations aren't returned. The parser strips the citation spans from `content`, and the document map can't go over JSON in `parse_context`.

reviews.body:
## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks @ldkhang1201 for picking this up. The fix looks right and covers what #65360 asked for. This has to wait for #64041 to land and then get a rebase. 

A few small suggestions:
- token_in_token_out/serving.py:756 keeps the output tokens even when there's no reasoning parser. Coupled chat only keeps them when the count gets reported, so the same guard would work here.
- The CompletionTokenUsageInfo block is repeated at online_derenderer.py:385 and :446 and could be a small helper.
- The e2e test never closes </think> within 32 tokens and the CPU helper hardcodes _include_reasoning_tokens_details = False. A stub parser unit test would be cheap and would cover both the closed block and the summing in the stream path.

Leaving continuous_usage_stats for a follow-up is fine.
